question: Does rainfall occurring only after the survey reproduce the same within-taxon concentration structure attributed to recent antecedent rain, consistent with a persistent wet-regime explanation rather than temporal specificity?
population: Intersection of the existing 2,916 strictly-prior-history pairs for which both survey runs have valid 72-h antecedent and non-overlapping 72-h future ERA5 precipitation windows.

weather.product: Same ERA5 hourly total precipitation source and route-run midpoint/coordinate procedure as the existing rain-amount common-environment analysis.
weather.antecedent_window: 72 hourly accumulations ending at the floored survey-midpoint hour, identical to the existing analysis.
weather.future_window: 72 hourly accumulations from +1 through +72 hours after the floored survey-midpoint hour; no hour overlaps the antecedent window.

model.baseline: Existing cross-fitted linear species response to DaysSinceRain with prior physical-site history, dry persistence and matched wet incidence.
model.antecedent_amount: Existing flexible cross-fitted species environment model with antecedent 72-h rainfall amount.
model.future_placebo: Exactly the same flexible model specification, replacing antecedent 72-h amount with future 72-h amount while retaining DaysSinceRain, temperature, season, State and RunNumber terms.
model.focal_endpoint: Existing conditional within-taxon concentration residual, with 1,000 simulations.
model.magnitude_conditioning: Observed total wet incidence is matched exactly; this remains a conditional spatial-allocation test.

primary_classification.future_placebo_sufficient: future-rain null does not exceed its upper 95% residual bound
primary_classification.future_placebo_rejected: future-rain null remains above its upper 95% residual bound

descriptive_comparison: Fraction of the same-sample baseline residual removed by antecedent amount.
Antecedent-minus-future residual-removal difference; descriptive only, with no retuned threshold.
interpretation_boundaries: This is a post-hoc negative control, not causal identification.
Future-rain association can arise from persistent wet spells or seasonality; failure of the placebo strengthens temporal specificity but does not prove rainfall causality.
DaysSinceRain remains in both amount models, so this tests incremental information in antecedent versus future rainfall amount beyond the existing recency term.
No window length, offset, endpoint, tail, sample rule or classification may change after results are read.
